stem: A client who has completed cancer treatment asks, 'Will I need routine CT scans forever to make sure the cancer does not come back?' Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Follow-up testing is individualized; the plan may include physical exams, laboratory tests, imaging, or other procedures based on the cancer, treatment received, overall health, and clinical findings.
options.B: Every cancer survivor needs the same lifelong CT schedule because surveillance imaging is standardized across all cancer types.
options.C: Once treatment ends, follow-up testing is unnecessary unless the client independently discovers a new mass.
options.D: Imaging replaces follow-up visits, so clinical assessment is no longer needed when routine scans are ordered.

rationale: A is correct. NCI states that all cancer survivors should receive follow-up care, but the follow-up schedule differs among patients based on factors such as cancer type, treatment received, and overall health. Follow-up visits may include physical examination, blood tests, imaging, and other necessary tests or procedures, and the specific tests and frequency are individualized. NCI also identifies monitoring for cancer recurrence as a valid use of imaging. B is incorrect because NCI does not support one standardized lifelong CT schedule for all survivors. C is incorrect because regular follow-up is recommended after treatment and clients should report new or persistent concerns rather than waiting for a mass. D is incorrect because imaging is one possible component of follow-up and does not replace clinical assessment and visits.
educational_objective: Explain that cancer surveillance after treatment is individualized and may include imaging when appropriate, rather than assuming that every survivor requires the same routine lifelong imaging schedule.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: Follow-Up Medical Care; NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms — follow-up care and follow-up care plan; Cancer Imaging Basics for Diagnosis and Treatment
source_version_date: Follow-Up Medical Care current NCI page accessed 2026-08-18; Cancer Imaging Basics reviewed 2026-07-28

source_claim_supported: All cancer survivors need follow-up care, but schedules and tests are individualized; follow-up may include exams, blood tests, imaging, and other procedures; imaging can be used to monitor for recurrence when clinically appropriate.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: monitor diagnostic testing, perform focused assessment, recognize trends/changes, and provide client education related to ordered testing and follow-up.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item because it overgeneralized scheduled surveillance imaging across cancers and implied a universal earlier-more-treatable-stage benefit. The final item reflects NCI guidance that follow-up is required but the tests, imaging use, and frequency are individualized.
audit_findings: Fresh NCI verification confirms that post-treatment follow-up is individualized by cancer type, treatment, overall health, and clinical needs.
NCI confirms that imaging may be used to monitor recurrence, but the source does not support a universal lifelong CT schedule for every survivor.
The unsafe universal claim that scheduled imaging is always intended to detect recurrence at an earlier, more treatable stage was removed.
All distractors are clinically plausible misconceptions and only A is defensible under the cited guidance.
Independent adversarial review found no second answer, cueing, unsupported imaging interval, source-locator defect, blueprint mismatch, or unresolved conflict.
